answer: Endorsement travels across a cut in the endorsement graph, and a cut is only real when the two sides have no common ancestor inside the endorsement horizon, so a cluster must be dissolved and rebuilt before its weight counts elsewhere. This cost is per identity, so it cannot be amortised across the fleet. The thread is the island, the beacon the endorsement that crosses it, and the voyage the shared ancestor that would disqualify the crossing; one thread is cheap to hold, but a beacon only counts when no voyage exists, and that takes independent history.
